title: Owner of Pilot Pete's Coffee and Treats, in Elmhurst Metra station, Peter Thomas, accused of selling methamphetamine: police

 Owner of coffee shop in Elmhurst Metra station accused of selling meth: police 
 The owner of Pilot Pete's Coffee and Treats in the Elmhurst Metra station, Peter Thomas, is accused of selling methamphetamine, police said. WLS By ABC7 Chicago Digital Team Friday, October 30, 2026 9:12PM Share Follow ABC7 on Google ELMHURST, Ill. (WLS) -- The owner of a coffee shop in Elmhurst's Metra station is facing charges of selling methamphetamine, ABC7 Chicago's news partner the Daily Herald reported .
 Peter Thomas, 35, of Villa Park was charged with selling methamphetamine to an undercover police officer three separate times, DuPage County State's Attorney Robert Berlin and Elmhurst Chief of Police Michael McLean said Thursday.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 He's been charged with intent to deliver methamphetamine, resisting a police officer and unlawful possession of marijuana by a driver, officials said.
 On Aug. 31, an undercover officer arranged to buy methamphetamine the next day at Thomas' business, Pilot Pete's Coffee and Treats, located in the 100-block of West First Street in Elmhurst, authorities allege.
 The officer bought the drugs at the business Sept. 1, officials say.

 According to prosecutors' petition, the methamphetamine was in a brown envelope labeled "Pilot Pete's Coffee & Treats."
 The officer made two more purchases Sept. 30 and Wednesday at Thomas' Villa Park home, officials said.
 Officials said Thomas was taken into custody Wednesday at his business and had methamphetamine in his pocket.
 Thomas appeared in court Thursday morning and was not detained pre-trial.
 He's been released with conditions including that he does not possess or consume alcohol, marijuana or any controlled substances other than those prescribed. He also must submit to testing.
 Thomas is next due in court Nov. 23.
